::: {#thm-pal-running-time}
#### A closed form for the running time of `pal`

Let $T(0) = T(1) = 1$ and $T(n) = T(n - 2) + 1$ for every integer $n \ge 2$, as in @exm-pal-running-time.
Then $T(n) = \floor{n / 2} + 1$ (@def-floor) for every non-negative integer (@def-nonnegative-integers) $n$.

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

The recurrence relation uses $T(n - 2)$, not $T(n - 1)$, so we use strong induction (@def-strong-induction).
Let $n \ge 0$ be an integer, and suppose $T(m) = \floor{m / 2} + 1$ for every integer $m$ with $0 \le m < n$.

If $n \le 1$, then $T(n) = 1 = 0 + 1 = \floor{n / 2} + 1$.

If $n \ge 2$, then $0 \le n - 2 < n$, and $\floor{(n - 2) / 2} = \floor{n / 2 - 1} = \floor{n / 2} - 1$,
since subtracting the integer 1 from a real number subtracts 1 from its floor.
So

$$
\ba
T(n)
&= T(n - 2) + 1
&& \text{(recurrence relation)}
\\&= \floor{(n - 2) / 2} + 1 + 1
&& \text{(strong induction hypothesis)}
\\&= \floor{n / 2} - 1 + 2
\\&= \floor{n / 2} + 1.
\ea
$$

So the formula holds for $n$, and by strong induction it holds for every non-negative integer $n$.

:::

:::
